The child closely preserves its document structure, statutory-notice paragraph, sequence of Cuba-specific justifications, and operative determination, with only updated dates and limited revisions to the factual framing. C21 and C02 are also close predecessors in the same drafting lineage, but C09 is the latest displayed letter with the closest language and the same set of four referenced amendments.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Section 202(d) of the National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1622(d)) provides for the automatic termination of a national emergency unless, within 90 days prior to the anniversary date of its declaration, the President publishes in the Federal Register and transmits to the Congress a notice stating that the emergency is to continue in effect beyond the anniversary date.","parent_excerpt":"Section 202(d) of the National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1622(d)) provides for the automatic termination of a national emergency unless, within 90 days before the anniversary date of its declaration, the President publishes in the Federal Register and transmits to the Congress a notice stating that the emergency is to continue in effect beyond the anniversary date.","explanation":"Nearly verbatim opening machinery, differing only in 'prior to' versus 'before.'"},{"child_excerpt":"The unauthorized entry of vessels subject to the jurisdiction of the United States into Cuban territorial waters is currently a violation of Federal law. Further, the unauthorized entry of United States-registered vessels into Cuban territorial waters continues to be detrimental to United States foreign policy and counter to the purpose of [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], which is to ensure, among other things, safe, orderly, and legal migration.","parent_excerpt":"The unauthorized entry of vessels subject to the jurisdiction of the United States into Cuban territorial waters is in violation of United States law and contrary to United States policy. Further, the unauthorized entry of United States-registered vessels into Cuban territorial waters continues to be detrimental to United States foreign policy and counter to the purpose of [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of May 24, 1992, which is to ensure, among other things, safe, orderly, and legal migration.","explanation":"Distinctive Cuba-specific language about unauthorized vessels and safe, orderly, and legal migration is substantially reproduced."},{"child_excerpt":"The possibility of large-scale unauthorized entries of United States-registered vessels into Cuban territorial waters would disturb the international relations of the United States regarding Cuba by allowing for or providing the means to facilitate a mass migration of Cuban nationals and threatening our national security.","parent_excerpt":"The possibility of large-scale unauthorized entries of United States-registered vessels would disturb the international relations of the United States by facilitating a possible mass migration of Cuban nationals.","explanation":"The child expands but plainly retains the parent's distinctive causal formulation connecting vessel entries, international relations, and Cuban mass migration."},{"child_excerpt":"Therefore, I have determined that it is necessary to continue the national emergency with respect to Cuba and the emergency authority relating
